memory_update.text: HSTM should be promoted for deeper Layer 2 review as the most direct underfollowed clinical-placement software and healthcare compliance-documentation asset found in this pass.
UTI is a relevant hands-on capacity operator because Concorde adds healthcare campus and clinical-placement exposure while legacy UTI adds trade-school lab and employer-partner exposure.

Clinical placement and simulation capacity are not pure online-learning exposures; the bottleneck appears to be offline throughput, compliance documentation, employer/health-system partnerships, and accredited lab capacity.

The most direct clinical-placement software assets are mostly private or embedded inside broader public companies; later layers should verify whether HSTM's acquired clinical-rotation products are financially material.

node: Clinical placement, apprenticeship administration, simulation labs, and hands-on training capacity
summary: Layer 1B expansion found a concentrated set of US-listed or US-traded public assets tied to the offline-capacity bottleneck in workforce education: clinical rotation software, healthcare workforce credentialing, nursing/healthcare school clinical partnerships, simulation hardware/software, and hands-on trade/healthcare campuses. The cleanest underfollowed node candidate is HealthStream because it directly acquired clinical rotation management assets and already serves healthcare workforce compliance/credentialing workflows. Universal Technical Institute is a hands-on capacity operator through transportation/skilled trades plus Concorde healthcare campuses. Adtalem is a more obvious healthcare-education reference name with direct clinical workforce partnerships. CAE is a simulation-capacity supplier, but healthcare is only a segment inside a broader aviation/defense simulation company, so its exposure should be treated as second-order.
